title: Tech Note: Reading a Full SOAP Request with 4th Dimension 2004
featured_technology: SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol) web services
4th Dimension native Web server SOAP publishing

historical_commentary.text: This note addresses an advanced SOAP web-services scenario in 4th Dimension 2004: reading a full, raw SOAP request directly (rather than relying on 4D's automatic XML-to-native-type binding) for debugging, logging, handling unbound inputs, or distinguishing empty values from absent ones. SOAP itself has become a largely obsolete web-services technology industry-wide, having been supplanted by REST/JSON APIs over the following decade, so while the note's underlying XML-parsing technique (DOM Parse XML) still exists in some form in 4D, the SOAP-specific context and motivation are now of primarily historical interest.
related_updates: SOAP-based web services have been broadly superseded across the industry by REST/JSON APIs
4D's own web services strategy has shifted to REST APIs built on ORDA rather than native SOAP publishing
Modern XML/JSON parsing in 4D has been substantially modernized since 2004, including native JSON support introduced in later versions
